item.title: Houthis threaten "painful" response if U.S. helps Saudis
item.description: As Trump mulls joining Saudi Arabia in attacking the Houthis, the Iran-backed group is threatening a "painful" response.

item.title: What we know as Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer, Vatican says | Special Report
item.description: The Vatican said Tuesday that Pope Leo has been diagnosed with lung cancer. Tony Dokoupil anchored CBS News' special report.

item.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer after undergoing surgery
item.description: Tests confirmed a diagnosis of lung cancer for Pope Leo XIV, the Vatican said in a medical update after he underwent surgery.

item.title: Extended interview: Grandmaster Flash on the creation of hip-hop, his new book and more
item.description: Grandmaster Flash speaks with Nate Burleson about his new book, "Birth of a Culture," where he gives readers an intimate look at his role in the birth of hip-hop.

item.title: Pope Leo diagnosed with lung cancer, Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo XIV has lung cancer and had the lower lobe of his right lung removed, the Vatican said on Tuesday. CBS News foreign correspondent Chris Livesay and University of Birmingham theology professor Candida Moss join to discuss.

item.title: Selma Blair arrested after allegedly biting flight attendant
item.description: Actress Selma Blair was arrested after an incident on board a Delta Air Lines flight from Los Angeles to John F. Kennedy International Airport Sunday night.

item.title: Duane "Keffe D" Davis sentenced to 40 years to life for Tupac's murder
item.description: Duane "Keffe D" Davis​ was sentenced to 40 years to life in prison Tuesday in Las Vegas for the 1996 murder of rapper Tupac Shakur.

item.title: Duane "Keffe D" Davis sentenced to 40 years to life for Tupac Shakur's murder
item.description: A judge sentenced Duane "Keffe D" Davis to 40 years to life for the murder of Tupac Shakur on Tuesday. CBS News legal reporter Katrina Kaufman has the details.

item.title: Pope Leo's lung nodule surgery completed successfully, Vatican says
item.description: Pope Leo XIV underwent a successful surgery Tuesday to remove a lung nodule, according to the Vatican.

item.title: Why AI could end the price tag as we know it
item.description: Retailers want to harness the power of artificial intelligence to set personalized prices for shoppers, a consumer protection expert says.

item.title: Engineer releases spycam footage of coworker allegedly poisoning her
item.description: A California engineer has released spycam footage of her coworker allegedly poisoning her. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul walks through the details of the case.

item.title: New details in text messages between Jane Doe and frat member
item.description: One of the accused fraternity members, who was later expelled, wrote to her: "I genuinely hope ur not catching as much heat from this as we r."

item.title: Judge blocks Trump admin. from felling trees at D.C. golf course
item.description: U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes blocked the Trump administration from cutting down trees at East Potomac Golf Links through Oct. 26.

item.title: Hackers raise temperatures on fridges in hundreds of French supermarkets
item.description: French investigators are on the hunt for hackers who raised temperatures on refrigerators at hundreds of supermarkets, sparking fires and food losses. CBS News reporter Inaya Folarin Iman has more.

item.title: Iran focused on attacking "harder targets," U.K. spy chief warns
item.description: Iran has made a "major shift" in its efforts to attack the United Kingdom, including going after harder targets such as military bases, the head of MI5 warned.

item.title: Is a bootleg weight-loss drug to blame for 2 reported deaths?
item.description: While unverified, the reports come amid growing efforts to clamp down on illicit sales of the experimental weight-loss drug retatrutide.

item.title: Controversy over new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia's legal credentials
item.description: Questions are rising over new White House press secretary Katie Zacharia's legal credentials and where she took her bar exam. CBS News' Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: Engineer releases video showing coworker adding substance into her drink, alleges she was poisoned
item.description: An engineer in Berkley, California, released spy camera footage of her coworker adding a substance to her drink. She alleges that he poisoned her for months. CBS News' Shanelle Kaul has the latest.

item.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle ousted as ambassador over corruption allegations
item.description: Kimberly Guilfoyle said she is stepping aside as U.S. ambassador to Greece, days after reports that she offered access to officials in exchange for help paying off her debt.

item.title: Character.ai declares bankruptcy, citing legal and business woes
item.description: AI company has faced multiple lawsuits from families who claimed their teenage children died by suicide or harmed themselves after using its platform.

item.title: Trump confirms Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation as U.S. ambassador to Greece
item.description: President Trump spoke with reporters Tuesday as he left the White House for his trip to Alaska. Trump confirmed Kimberly Guilfoyle's resignation as U.S. ambassador to Greece, saying, "She will not be there. I didn't like what I read."

item.title: Bootleg weight-loss drug linked to 2 recent deaths, CBS News investigation finds
item.description: Two recent deaths reported to the FDA could be linked to Retatrutide, an unapproved weight-loss drug made popular on social media. CBS News investigative reporter Daniel Gilbert has the latest.

item.title: Bipartisan senators call Russia diesel deal a "betrayal" of Ukraine
item.description: A bipartisan group of senators urged President Trump to withdraw from his diesel deal with Russian President Vladimir Putin and rescind a move to waive sanctions on Russia's energy sector.

item.title: Kimberly Guilfoyle says she's resigning as U.S. ambassador to Greece
item.description: Kimberly Guilfoyle said Tuesday she's resigning as the U.S. ambassador to Greece after an associate claimed she asked him to wire $100,000 to her American Express account. CBS News' Nancy Cordes has more.

item.title: Six Flags closes 9 rides across 6 parks after deadly incident
item.description: Six Flags has temporarily closed rides similar to Goliath, the roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia that a man fell from.

item.title: Mark Harmon and Austin Stowell on playing Leroy Jethro Gibbs in "NCIS" | Between Us
item.description: Mark Harmon, who played Leroy Jethro Gibbs for 18 seasons on "NCIS," sits down with Austin Stowell, who plays the younger version of Gibbs on "NCIS: Origins," to talk about playing the iconic character, reflect on the start of their acting careers and what's in store for Season 3 of the prequel series.

item.title: Is a College Degree Even Worth the Money Anymore? | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: Is a $400K tuition bill really worth it for four years of partying? Jill and Mark break down how to get the most value out of your college degree, and when it might not be worth the price at all. Plus, caller Michael wants to know whether he can realistically afford the home renovation he's been eyeing.

item.title: Would access to Russian diesel help drive down U.S. prices?
item.description: Average U.S. diesel prices remain stuck above $6 a gallon, raising fuel costs in trucking, agriculture and construction.

item.title: Hackers heat up refrigerators at hundreds of supermarkets
item.description: The cyberattack caused refrigerators to shoot up in temperature in hundreds of stores, sparking fires and forcing spoiled food to be thrown away.

item.title: Evidence in the Amy Mullis corn rake murder case
item.description: A look inside the case against Todd Mullis, a Iowa farmer accused of killing his wife with a farm tool.
